newsitem.title: UK: Rank H1 to show effects of poor trading.
newsitem.headline: Rank H1 to show effects of poor trading.

text.p: Disappointing trading is set to depress first half earnings from British leisure company Rank Group Plc as the benefits of a radical resturcturing take time to feed through, analysts said.

Pre-tax profit is forecast at 90-98 million stg, against an adjusted first half figure of 99 million last year, when Rank reports on Thursday. Interim dividend is seen at 5.0-5.4p, against 5.0p at this stage in 1996.
Rank shares have underperformed the stock market by some 40 percent over the past 12 months, testimony to scepticism about the strategy of chief executive Andrew Teare.

Teare, who joined Rank in April 1996, has raised 1.3 billion stg from disposals, including the sale of the company's remaining 20 percent stake in the Rank Xerox office equipment venture to Xerox Corporation in a deal worth up to 1.0 billion stg.
Rank intends to use some of the proceeds to buy back up to 250 million stg of its own shares.
The company is focusing on four areas of activity -- Film and Entertainment Services, Hard Rock, Holidays and Leisure.
But fresh doubts were raised about Teare's strategy by a trading update in June, which showed that underlying growth in turnover was just one percent in the first five months of the year.
One of the main causes for concern was a decline in profit from video duplication, volumes in the U.S. falling 25 percent.
Broker Lehman Brothers, who recently downgraded the stock to "neutral" from "outperform", said Rank may need an acquisition to revive its flagging fortunes.
"...The amount of time necessary for an earnings turnaround from existing businesses is likely to be long, leaving an acquisition necessary to restore momentum," it said in a research note.
Much of Rank's business is weighted towards the second half and the current consensus forecast for full-year profit is 333 million stg.
